tech.engine_status:
Read on godotengine.org on 13 Nov 2026: latest stable is 4.7.2 (18 Aug 2026). 4.8 is at beta 3 (9 Nov 2026, feature-frozen; adds Jolt 5.6.0, non-allocating physics queries, mip-level texture streaming, screen-space contact shadows). Stay on 4.7.2 and revisit at 4.8.1.

Relevant additions:
- 4.4: Jolt built in (experimental), 3D physics interpolation, AgX, ubershaders.
- 4.5: stencil buffer, shader baker, SMAA, interpolation moved into SceneTree.
- 4.6: Jolt default for new 3D projects, rewritten SSR, D3D12 default on Windows, IK framework, Tracy.
- 4.7: AreaLight3D, HDR output, Asset Store.

Jolt in 4.7 (docs and source):
- Only "run on separate thread" is still experimental; some joint soft limits are unsupported.
- Defaults are max_bodies 10240, max_body_pairs 65536, max_contact_constraints 20480; overflow drops contacts with a one-time warning.
- One collision step per tick; jobs use all WorkerThreadPool threads.
- No neighbour wake-up when a body is removed; compounds are rebuilt in full on any shape change; convex hulls max 256 points; no state save/restore exposed.

Forward+ offers SDFGI (semi-dynamic), VoxelGI, SSIL, SSAO, SSR, volumetric fog and FogVolume, TAA, FSR 1.0/2.2, decals, GPU particles with real-time box/sphere/heightfield collision (SDF collision is baked), CPU occlusion culling, visibility ranges, auto mesh LOD, automatic instancing, MultiMesh with interpolation and compute shaders. HDDAGI (SDFGI successor, PR 86267) has been a locked draft since Dec 2024.

Rigid bodies on this CPU (my estimate, to be measured in spike 1): 1,500-2,500 awake simple debris bodies at 60 Hz within 6-8 ms; 10-20k total if the rest sleep.

approaches.name: a. Full voxel world (Teardown-style '3D pixel sandbox')
approaches.how_it_works: Every object is a small voxel volume. Teardown stores one byte per voxel (256-entry palette) in a 3D texture per object, rasterises only the bounding box and ray-marches inside it, keeps a world-scale 1-bit shadow volume (262 MB on one level) for traced lighting, and splits objects into new objects by connected components when voxels are removed (https://acko.net/blog/teardown-frame-teardown/). In Godot this means: voxelise imported GLBs offline, then either a custom ray-march renderer or greedy-meshed chunks, custom voxel rigid bodies (compound boxes in Jolt) and a 3D flood fill after every edit. Existing pieces: godot_voxel blocky terrain (one world-aligned static grid, .vox import, no voxel rigid bodies; separate_floating_chunks exists only for smooth LOD terrain) and the 'Voxel Destruction' add-on (.vox objects drawn as MultiMesh cubes, GDScript with optional Rust, v1.2.1, MIT).
pros: One uniform rule: everything breaks the same way, ground and strata included
Stylised look hides the missing artist; proven fun
Destruction state is plain data, so saving and rewinding are simple
cons: No engine support in Godot: renderer, voxel physics and island splitting would all be custom engine-level work
Flood fill and meshing are far beyond GDScript; needs C++ or Rust
Asset-pack models lose their detail at 10-25 cm voxels: fails 'real 3D models' and 'realistic'
Jolt has no voxel shape: each body becomes hundreds of box sub-shapes; heavy on RAM and VRAM
approaches.fit: Real asset-pack models: poor (everything is re-voxelised). Realistic look: no, stylised only. Strata digging: excellent. Performance on this machine: unknown, high risk. Implementable by an AI agent without native code: no.
approaches.perf_notes: 1 km x 1 km x 60 m at 10 cm is 6e11 cells, so sparse storage and streaming are mandatory. A 64^3 flood fill is about 260k cells x 6 neighbours: tens of ms in GDScript per edit (estimate).
approaches.verdict: Reject as the basis of the world. Technical answer to the style question: do not go full voxel in Godot. Optional use: the Voxel Destruction add-on for a few 'glitched simulation' props near the world edge.

approaches.name: b. Pre-fractured pieces swapped in on damage + connectivity graph
approaches.how_it_works: Offline, every destructible piece (modular wall/floor/roof module, prop, vehicle part) is cut into 8-20 shards along Voronoi cells; cut faces get an interior material and each shard gets a convex collider. At runtime the intact piece is hidden and pooled shard bodies appear at the same transforms; a graph (pieces as nodes, shared faces as edges, ground anchors) decides which neighbours lose support. Ways to produce shards: Blender Cell Fracture headless (extension v0.2.1, Blender 4.2+, GPL, needs a Blender install); pure Python with trimesh + manifold3d + scipy (pip only); in-editor VoronoiShatter (GDScript, editor-time, needs manifold input, self-described 'highly experimental'); Destronoi (Godot 4.2.x, convex meshes only, no UVs on fragments); godot-destruction-plugin (only the swap step). Robust variant for non-watertight asset meshes: clip the piece's triangles by the cell planes and build the interior caps from a solid convex proxy of the piece instead of using mesh booleans.
pros: Zero runtime geometry cost; fully deterministic, so easy to test, save and rewind
Shards of a piece type share meshes: automatic instancing in Forward+ and pooled bodies
Exterior keeps the real asset-pack surface; interiors get a triplanar material
Pure scripts: an agent can generate and validate it offline (volume and watertightness checks)
cons: Pattern is not impact-specific; needs 3-4 variants per piece plus rotation and mirroring to hide repetition
A downloaded whole building (one hollow shell) still cannot collapse structurally: buildings must be modular
The Godot add-ons found are small and experimental; expect to own the pipeline
More mesh memory (shard sets per piece type)
approaches.fit: Real asset-pack models: good for props, vehicles and modular kit pieces. Realistic look: good with interior materials plus rebar and dust dressing. Strata: not applicable. Performance: best of all options. AI-agent implementability: good.
approaches.perf_notes: Runtime cost per fracture is a pool pop plus about 10 server calls per shard (well under 0.1 ms per piece, estimate). The budget is set by awake bodies, not by geometry.
approaches.verdict: Adopt as the geometry source for all man-made objects: every fracture pattern is precomputed by an offline Python pipeline.

approaches.name: c. Runtime convex fracture on structural elements + stress/support graph (Red Faction Guerrilla style)
approaches.how_it_works: Buildings are assemblies of solid convex elements: floor slabs in roughly 3 m panels, wall panels split around openings, columns, beams, roof panels. Each element has material, mass, health and edges to touching neighbours; foundations are anchors. Damage splits the hit element into convex cells biased toward the impact (a Voronoi cell is an intersection of bisector half-spaces; Geometry3D.compute_convex_mesh_points, clip_polygon and tetrahedralize_delaunay are native in 4.7). Cells near the hit detach, the rest stay as static sub-elements. A BFS from the anchors over intact edges then finds unsupported clusters, which become compound rigid bodies; a load-versus-capacity heuristic breaks overloaded supports for progressive collapse. Clusters break further on hard impacts.
pros: Impact-specific holes and believable structural collapse (pancaking, toppling)
Convex-only maths is robust: no mesh booleans, and the cell is its own collider
Small, testable code; the graph has hundreds of nodes, not millions of voxels
Digging under foundations can remove anchors, giving emergent collapses
cons: Runtime mesh and hull creation costs about 1-3 ms per element in GDScript (estimate) and produces unique meshes that defeat instancing
Buildings must be generated as elements; arbitrary downloaded building meshes cannot be used as-is
Stress heuristics need tuning to avoid floating bits or endless chain reactions
Godot's Jolt module rebuilds a whole compound on any shape change: use one body per element or small compounds
approaches.fit: Real asset-pack models: medium (elements are kit modules or PBR panels; props and dressing are real models). Realistic look: high. Strata: no. Performance: good with budgets. AI-agent implementability: good (pure code, automatable tests).
approaches.perf_notes: BFS over a 500-2,000 element building in typed GDScript with packed adjacency: about 1-5 ms (estimate), run on WorkerThreadPool and only for buildings hit that frame. A 5-storey 15 m building is about 500 elements; a 30-storey tower about 7,000.
approaches.verdict: Adopt the structure model (elements, anchors, support graph, load heuristic). Take the geometry from (b); use true runtime Voronoi only for glass and for the single element under a hero impact, inside a per-frame ms budget.

approaches.name: d. Smooth voxel/SDF ground with strata (Voxel Tools / godot_voxel), combined with b+c for structures
approaches.how_it_works: The ground is a signed distance field meshed with Transvoxel: VoxelLodTerrain + VoxelMesherTransvoxel. VoxelTool.do_sphere, do_path and grow_sphere carve it at runtime; each 16^3 block gets a threaded mesh and a static trimesh collider. Strata are drawn by a triplanar shader keyed on depth below the original surface (sub-base, soil, clay, rock, bedrock, magma), and dig resistance is looked up from the same depth; per-voxel texture indices ('Single' or 'Mixel4' modes) exist if painted materials are needed. Thin hard layers (asphalt, pavement, kerbs) are plate elements from b/c lying on the SDF, so they crack into slabs before the soil is dug. VoxelTool.copy and paste give before/after buffers for rewind; modified blocks persist through a VoxelStream (SQLite or region files). Foundations query the SDF beneath them and lose their anchor when it is dug away.
pros: Real craters, trenches and tunnels with overhangs
Native C++ and threaded, with a prebuilt Windows binary and no toolchain: GodotVoxelExtension.zip v1.7x 'for Godot 4.5+' (20 Aug 2026, MIT, 18.5k downloads)
No-compile fallback: prebuilt 'Godot 4.7.2 + Voxel Tools 1.7' Windows editor and release export template
Saving and undoing edits are supported by the API
cons: The author says the GDExtension build 'hasn't gone through much testing'; tracker issue #442 is still open
Voxel size is 1 unit (scale the node for 0.5 m); 10 cm layers cannot be geometric
Collider builds run on the main thread, time-sliced, at about 3-5x the meshing cost: latency under heavy digging
Edits and collisions exist only near viewers unless full-load mode is on (more memory)
separate_floating_chunks is expensive (advised box about 30 voxels)
approaches.fit: Real models: neutral (ground is procedural). Realistic look: good with PBR triplanar and depth bands. Strata: yes, the only practical route found. Performance: good near the player. AI-agent implementability: good (GDScript API, no native code).
approaches.perf_notes: 1 km^2 at 0.5 m is 2048 x 2048 x about 128 voxels; only edited blocks are stored. Keep voxel/threads/main/time_budget_ms around 4-6 ms (default about 8) and batch edits with collision_update_delay.
approaches.verdict: Adopt for the ground. If spike 3 fails on both the extension and the module build, fall back to a 2.5D heightfield (craters and trenches, no tunnels) with the same depth-banded shader.

approaches.name: e. Supplements: GPU compute, slicing, render-only damage, canned far-field collapse
approaches.how_it_works: (1) Compute shaders through RenderingDevice for cosmetic simulation only (dust, tens of thousands of chips). (2) Plane slicing for a claw or laser power: Godot 4 Concave Mesh Slicer (CSG-based, cross-section material, MIT) or Mesh Tools slice_mesh. (3) Shell-shard fracture for sheet metal: cut thin vehicle shells by planes without caps, double-sided material. (4) Render-only damage: decals, a crack overlay driven by a per-instance uniform, a stencil or discard 'hole' shader for small hits. (5) Canned collapse for buildings outside the simulation bubble: shader-driven sink and crumble plus dust, then swap to a ruin proxy. (6) Rubble absorption: old piles are added back into the SDF terrain as mounds.
pros: Each item is small, optional and independent
Cheap ways to add visible damage where full simulation is not affordable
Slicing gives a distinct power with little code
cons: Compute readback takes 2-3 frames and long dispatches can trigger a Windows driver timeout (Godot docs), so gameplay must not depend on it
CSG-based slicing needs reasonably clean meshes
Render-only damage has no physical effect and must be reconciled when real damage follows
approaches.fit: Supports the 'realistic feel' and performance goals; does not by itself satisfy 'everything destructible' or strata.
approaches.perf_notes: GPU particles collide in real time only with box, sphere and heightfield colliders; SDF particle collision is baked in the editor and therefore useless for a changing world.
approaches.verdict: Use as supplements. Nothing found beats b+c+d as the core.

tech.gdscript_performance:
Not for per-voxel or per-triangle inner loops; yes as orchestration. Rule of thumb (not measured here): typed GDScript is roughly 50-100x slower than C++ in tight loops, and the Voxel Tools docs say GDScript is too slow for heavy voxel loops.

Recommended path: GDScript-first, with every hot path routed to one of these.
1. Native engine calls: Jolt, Geometry3D.clip_polygon / compute_convex_mesh_points / tetrahedralize_delaunay, ArrayMesh, automatic instancing, MultiMesh.
2. One prebuilt native extension: Voxel Tools for terrain meshing and collision.
3. Offline Python (trimesh, manifold3d, scipy, coacd) that precomputes shard sets, colliders, adjacency graphs and HLOD proxies.
4. Small graph jobs in GDScript on WorkerThreadPool with packed CSR adjacency, results applied on the main thread under a per-frame ms budget.

Debris must be pooled unscripted RigidBody3D nodes so transform sync stays in C++; never run one GDScript callback per body per tick.

Other options:
- Compute shaders: cosmetic effects only (readback takes 2-3 frames, driver-timeout risk on long dispatches).
- C#: needs the .NET editor build and SDK and cannot call GDExtension classes natively (only Call/Get/Set). Keep it as escape hatch 1 for a pure-math loop that misses its budget; the dotnet CLI suits an agent and fails with exceptions, not crashes.
- C++ or Rust GDExtension: escape hatch 2 (toolchain install, crash debugging without a human).

Thread rules from the docs: the scene tree is not thread-safe; PhysicsServer is thread-safe only with the experimental separate-thread setting; build resources off-thread and attach them on the main thread. Benchmark exported release builds only.
tech.recommended_stack:
Engine: Godot 4.7.2 standard build, Forward+ (D3D12 default; keep Vulkan as a launch option), built-in Jolt, typed GDScript and gdshader, physics at 60 Hz with physics interpolation on.

- Ground: Voxel Tools GDExtension 1.7x, VoxelLodTerrain + Transvoxel, 0.5 m voxels, bounded to about 1 km2. Strata come from a depth-banded triplanar shader; hardscape (asphalt, pavement) is plate elements on top; a no-dig mask protects trees.
- Structures: buildings generated from modular structural elements (CC0 kit modules or PBR panels), each with a convex proxy, precomputed shard sets, an auto-built adjacency graph and ground anchors. Runtime is damage, shard swap, support BFS plus load heuristic, and unsupported clusters as compound rigid bodies.
- Props, vehicles, NPCs, animals, trees: real asset-pack GLB models. Vehicles and props are part-based with precomputed shell shards; humans ragdoll; animals and nature sit on an invulnerable layer.
- Debris: three tiers (convex clusters; pooled auto-instanced chunks with no debris-debris collision; GPU particles plus FogVolume dust). Rubble persists as static instances or SDF mounds.
- Rewind: 30 Hz transform ring buffer, inverse event log and voxel before-buffers over a 30 s window.
- World: 64 m streaming cells, element-level simulation inside a 120-150 m bubble, merged HLOD proxies with visibility ranges beyond.
- Save: destroyed-element bitsets per building, the Voxel Tools modified-block stream, and player/progress JSON.
- Offline pipeline: Python 3.13 with trimesh, manifold3d, scipy and coacd (pip only).

No Blender, no C# and no custom C++ unless a spike fails; if one does, try C# first.
tech.rewind_design:
Physics cannot run backwards and Godot does not expose Jolt's save/restore state, so record and replay: a state ring buffer plus an invertible event log (the Braid approach; Red Faction Guerrilla's Reconstructor is the precedent for debris flying back).

Record:
- Every second physics tick (30 Hz), store position (3 x f32) and rotation (quaternion) for awake tracked bodies only; sleeping bodies write nothing. Velocities are derived at resume.
- Event log, timestamped and invertible: element fractured, cluster detached, body spawned or retired, terrain edit (VoxelTool.copy before-buffer, restored with paste), NPC and vehicle state changes.
- Anything destroyed inside the window is only hidden and pooled; it is freed when its event leaves the window.

Memory for 2,000 bodies over 30 s:
- 60 Hz full state (52 B per sample): 187 MB.
- 30 Hz position + quaternion in f32 (28 B): 50 MB.
- 20 Hz quantised (10 B): 12 MB.
- With sleep skipping, typically under 10 MB.

Playback: turn tracked bodies into non-colliding static ghosts, drive visuals by lerp/slerp between samples at -1x to -4x, and apply inverse events as time crosses them. Physics cost while rewinding is near zero.

Resume, in this order: set BODY_STATE_TRANSFORM; switch to RIGID; write velocities (Jolt zeroes them on entering kinematic mode); re-apply SLEEPING (a teleport wakes the body); reset physics interpolation; discard the future.

Pitfalls:
- Kinematic ghosts push live bodies; use static no-collision ghosts.
- Wake bodies in the affected AABB by hand, because Jolt does not wake neighbours.
- Pool bodies and shapes; avoid create/free bursts.
- Raise the Jolt limits.
- The re-simulated future diverges from the original (acceptable).
- Restored terrain edits cause re-mesh and collider bursts; cap them per frame.
performance_tactics: Frame budget at 60 fps (16.6 ms): physics <= 6 ms, destruction logic <= 2 ms, other scripts <= 2 ms, render submission <= 4 ms on CPU; GPU <= 14 ms. Log Performance monitors (physics time, active 3D physics objects, draw calls, video memory) in every automated run.

Three debris tiers with hard caps: T1 structural clusters and large shards (boxes or convex hulls of <= 16 points; <= 400 awake), T2 pooled canonical chunks (24-32 shapes, box colliders; <= 1,200 awake), T3 chips and dust as GPU particles (no bodies). Over budget, demote the oldest, smallest and farthest: T1 to T2 to frozen rubble to particle.

Collision layers: T2 does not collide with T2 (removes pile contacts, the dominant solver cost); T3 collides only with the particle heightfield; the player collides with T1 and sleeping T2; animals and trees sit on an invulnerable layer.

Raise Jolt limits before any test: max_bodies 65536, max_body_pairs 262144, max_contact_constraints 65536, temporary buffer 128 MiB. At the defaults, overflow silently drops contacts. Lower velocity_steps from 10 to 6-8 and raise sleep_velocity_threshold from 0.03 to 0.1-0.2 m/s only if stacks stay stable.

Sleep aggressively: force debris asleep when slower than 0.2 m/s for 0.3 s outside 30 m. After removing any support, wake bodies in its AABB manually (shape query, then sleeping = false), because Jolt does not wake neighbours.

Rubble must persist without bodies: sleeping debris beyond budget becomes static instances; old or far piles are absorbed into the SDF terrain as rubble mounds (VoxelTool add mode), so nothing visibly vanishes.

Debris as pooled, unscripted RigidBody3D + MeshInstance3D nodes sharing a few meshes and materials: Forward+ automatically instances identical opaque mesh+material pairs and the transform sync stays in C++.
Intact elements: static bodies created through PhysicsServer3D RIDs with shared BoxShape3D, drawn as one MultiMesh per (building, piece type); removing an element is a swap-remove of one instance.
One body per element or small compounds (<= 32 shapes): Godot's Jolt module rebuilds the entire compound on every shape add or remove.
Time-slice everything: a fracture/graph queue with a ms budget per frame, so collapses propagate over several frames (this also reads as progressive failure). Graph BFS runs on WorkerThreadPool.
Shed load with slow motion: physics 60 Hz, max physics steps per frame 2, physics interpolation on; when physics exceeds budget, lower Engine.time_scale to 0.5-0.7 instead of dropping frames.

Simulation bubble and streaming: 64 m cells; element-level bodies and visuals only within about 120-150 m of the player; beyond that one merged proxy mesh per building with visibility ranges and no dynamic bodies; far collapses are canned (shader crumble plus dust, then a ruin proxy rebuilt on a worker thread).

Culling and shadows: one primitive BoxOccluder3D per intact building core, hidden once the building is damaged (toggling visibility is cheap, moving or rebaking occluders is not). T2 debris casts shadows only within about 30 m, T3 never; directional shadow distance about 150 m.
Continuous collision detection only on thrown projectiles; contact monitoring only on T1 clusters and thrown bodies (for impact damage), never on T2.
Terrain: mesh block size 16, collision_update_delay to batch edits, main-thread voxel budget 4-6 ms, a cap on dig edits per second, colliders only around the player viewer.
Benchmark exported release builds only (GDScript and Voxel Tools are much slower under the editor debugger); profile with the built-in profiler or Tracy (supported since 4.6).
tech.climbing_and_grabbing:
Climbing: CharacterBody3D with a capsule and a state machine (Ground, Air, Climb, Mantle, Ride).
- Enter when a forward sphere cast hits a climbable collider (layers: structure, terrain, trees; debris only if asleep and heavy) at 45-135 degrees from up.
- While climbing: floating motion mode, no gravity, input moves along the wall's tangent plane. Every physics tick, probe with 4-5 rays (centre plus paws) along the inverse normal, smooth the averaged normal, snap to hit point + normal x (radius + skin), and align the model by slerp.
- Outer corners: if the forward probe misses, cast back around the edge. Inner corners: blend to the new wall normal. Ledges: ray down from above and ahead, mantle if walkable.
- Destruction safety: store the collider RID and a local anchor, and revalidate every tick. If the collider is gone, go to Air with inherited velocity. If it became a falling cluster, Ride in its local space until its angular speed passes a threshold. Never trust a cached surface for more than one tick.
- Paws: use the 4.6 IK modifiers (TwoBoneIK3D, FABRIK3D) for placement, since free packs have no climbing animations.

Grab and throw:
- Pick by sphere cast from the camera among debris bodies under a mass cap, with a stencil outline highlight. Intact elements are first detached through the normal damage path.
- Hold with a velocity drive, not parenting or teleporting: each tick v = clamp((target - position) x k), angular velocity toward the target orientation, gravity scale 0, collision exception with the player, auto-drop if the error stays large. This sidesteps the joint soft limits Jolt does not support.
- Throw: restore gravity, apply an impulse along the aim, enable CCD for about 1 s, and monitor contacts (4) on the projectile only, to turn impact into damage. Remove the collision exception after 0.2 s.
tech.rendering_plan:
Base: Forward+ at native 1080p with TAA (or FSR 2.2 at scale 1.0 as anti-aliasing; FSR 2.2 at about 77% as the performance preset); shader baker on export.

GI: nothing in Godot is correct for a world that changes shape. SDFGI is the only city-scale option, but per the docs removed static meshes stay in the field until the camera leaves the cascade or SDFGI is toggled. HDDAGI is unmerged; VoxelGI and LightmapGI are baked.
- High preset: SDFGI (4 cascades, half resolution, occlusion on) + SSIL + SSAO, with a forced SDFGI off/on refresh hidden in the dust of a major collapse.
- Medium preset: sky ambient + SSAO + SSIL + ReflectionProbes re-captured after big changes.
- Decide the default in spike 5.

Light and post: one DirectionalLight3D (4 splits, PCSS); physical or custom sky shader with time of day (Sky3D as a starting point); AgX tonemapping, glow, auto exposure, SSR for wet surfaces and glass, colour-grading LUT. Vignette, grain and chromatic aberration go in one full-screen shader. Motion blur only via an add-on.

Dust: volumetric fog (low global density, temporal reprojection) plus up to about 12 pooled FogVolumes with an animated-noise fog shader for lingering clouds. Fast dust and chips are lit GPUParticles3D colliding with a camera-following heightfield.

Materials: triplanar PBR from CC0 sets for structural pieces and fracture interiors; a per-instance damage uniform driving a crack overlay; decals for scorch marks; instanced rebar on concrete break faces; the depth-banded strata shader.

Not available in Godot 4.7: Nanite-class geometry, Lumen-class or ray-traced GI and reflections, built-in DLSS/XeSS, built-in motion blur, order-independent transparency, volumetric clouds, smoke or fluid simulation, texture streaming (arrives in 4.8), hair or fur grooms.
tech.engine_alternatives: Recommendation: stay on Godot 4.7.2 and accept a lower visual ceiling than UE5; revisit only if spikes 1-3 fail. On paper Unreal Engine 5 is materially better: Chaos Destruction ships the system we must hand-build (Geometry Collections, clustering, a connection graph with strain, physics fields, Niagara hooks, cache replay), and Lumen and Nanite address dynamic GI and geometry density. For this production it is the wrong choice. Its assets are binary .uasset files and fracturing is authored in the Fracture Mode editor GUI, so an agent limited to text files and CLIs would have to drive everything through editor Python, commandlets and C++, with long compile times and a very large toolchain; diggable strata terrain is not a stock feature; Chaos plus Lumen is heavy for an 8 GB laptop GPU; and nobody is available to tune it visually. Unity 6 is closer to agent-friendly (YAML scenes and prefabs, C# for fast loops, Personal tier free up to USD 200k revenue with the runtime fee cancelled), but it has no built-in destruction, the capable destruction tools are paid assets against a zero budget, its GUID-wired YAML is brittle to hand-write, and it requires an account. Neither engine removes the real cost driver, which is content built specifically for destruction. Godot is MIT-licensed, fully text-native (scenes, resources, shaders, scripts), runs headless from the CLI, has Jolt built in and a prebuilt voxel terrain extension.
risks: Voxel terrain dependency: the Voxel Tools GDExtension 1.7x is flagged by its author as little tested, its GDExtension tracker issue (#442) is still open, and it has one maintainer. Mitigation: spike 3 soak test; fallback A is the prebuilt module build (4.7.2 editor + Windows release template), fallback B is heightfield digging.

The destruction system is the whole game and has no off-the-shelf Godot equivalent (the add-ons found are small or experimental). Typical failures are floating pieces, buildings that refuse to fall and chain reactions that never stop; it needs automated island and energy checks in scripted test runs.
Jolt behaviour under load: large piles of convex debris can jitter or overflow contact buffers, sleeping bodies are not woken when supports vanish, and the thread-safe mode is experimental.
GDScript ceiling: if runtime Voronoi, graph or recorder loops miss their budgets, the fallback is C# (.NET editor build + SDK) or a native extension, both adding toolchain and stability risk.
Lighting: SDFGI goes stale after destruction and no engine-side fix is in 4.7 or the 4.8 beta; without GI, street canyons look flat.
GPU memory: 8 GB VRAM with SDFGI, volumetric fog, 4-split shadows and many PBR sets, with no texture streaming before 4.8. Fix texture budgets (1K-2K) from the start.

'AAA in every respect' is not reachable with no artist or animator, mixed CC0 packs (style clash), limited cat animation sets and no bespoke audio. The defensible promise is AAA-feeling destruction feedback inside one coherent stylised-realistic look.

Asset fit: downloaded building models are hollow shells and cannot collapse structurally, so buildings must be assembled from modular pieces. Sketchfab models carry mixed licences (CC-BY, non-commercial) and inconsistent scale and polygon budgets.
Agent blind spots: visual quality, game feel and physical plausibility cannot be judged from text. The project needs an automated screenshot and video capture loop and regular review by the director.
Rewind edge cases: NPC, vehicle and AI state, particles, audio, terrain re-mesh bursts, and objects created and destroyed inside the window. A local (partial) rewind multiplies inconsistencies.
Scope: open world, NPCs, vehicles, many powers, rewind and saving on top of full destruction. Without vertical-slice gating the project stalls; the Steam minimum spec will be CPU-heavy.
Version churn: 4.8 stable is close (new Jolt version and physics query API). Pin 4.7.2 and the matching Voxel Tools build per milestone.
Licence hygiene: MIT notices for add-ons, no GPL code in the shipped game (Blender and Cell Fracture are tools only), and a manifest recording the licence of every asset.
spike_plan: S1 Jolt debris budget (1-2 days). Scripted benchmark in a release export, no gameplay: drop 1k/2k/4k/8k pooled unscripted RigidBody3D (boxes vs 12-point hulls, 3 shared meshes) onto static boxes and onto a pile; variants with debris-debris collision on/off and raised limits; then delete the floor under a sleeping pile. Log physics ms, frame ms and active bodies to JSON. PASS: >= 2,000 awake boxes and >= 1,000 awake hulls with physics <= 6 ms and frame <= 16.6 ms (p95) at 1080p with shadows; no 'contacts were ignored' warnings; the manual wake makes the pile fall. FAIL: lower the caps, use boxes only, or reopen the engine question.

S2 Offline fracture pipeline + one structural building (4-6 days). Python (trimesh, manifold3d, scipy) turns 10 CC0 modular kit pieces into a convex proxy, 3 shard sets (clipped triangles + capped interiors), colliders and adjacency. Godot assembles a 5-storey, ~500-element building with ground anchors, support BFS, load heuristic and tiered debris. Scripted tests: (a) hole in a 3rd-floor wall, (b) remove all ground-floor columns, (c) 20 random blasts. PASS: shard-set volume within 2% of the proxy for 10/10 pieces; no visible pop in intact-vs-fractured A/B screenshots; (a) building stands; (b) full collapse within 10 s; after settling no intact element lacks a path to an anchor (automated); frame <= 16.6 ms p95 and <= 25 ms p99 during (b); graph work <= 2 ms per frame.

S3 Diggable strata terrain (2-3 days). Stock 4.7.2 + GodotVoxelExtension 1.7x: bounded 512 m VoxelLodTerrain, 0.5 m voxels, depth-banded triplanar strata shader, do_sphere digging at 10 edits/s, 200 rigid bodies resting on edited ground, a building anchor that fails when the SDF under it is removed, save/load of modified blocks, Windows release export with standard templates. PASS: loads in editor and exported build; 30-minute scripted dig soak without crash or error spam; crater visible and collidable <= 100 ms after the edit; >= 60 fps while digging; no body tunnels through edited ground; save/load round trip identical. FAIL: repeat with the module build (v1.7 editor + template); if that fails, heightfield fallback.

S4 Rewind (3-4 days) on the S2+S3 scene: 30 Hz ring-buffer recorder for awake bodies, inverse event log including voxel before-buffers. Destroy for 30 s, rewind fully at 2x, resume, destroy again. PASS: recorder <= 1 ms average per physics tick with 2,000 tracked bodies; memory <= 64 MB; after a full rewind every element transform is within 1 mm of its initial state, the support graph is identical and the voxel hash is identical (automated diff); no body exceeds its recorded speed by more than 20% in the first second after resume; frame <= 16.6 ms during rewind.

S5 Look and lighting slice (3-4 days). One street block of S2 buildings with CC0 PBR triplanar materials, sky and sun, volumetric fog, FogVolume dust, GPU particles with heightfield collision, TAA, AgX, glow. Preset A: SDFGI + SSIL + SSAO. Preset B: SSIL + SSAO + probes. Scripted fly-through with a collapse; capture frame times, video memory and before/after stills and video. PASS: preset A holds >= 60 fps (GPU <= 14 ms) at native 1080p during the collapse with video memory <= 6 GB; the director accepts the stills; stale-GI artefacts after the collapse are acceptable or cured by the SDFGI off/on refresh. Otherwise preset B becomes the default.

S6 Climb and grab on a collapsing building (3-4 days). Cat controller with climb, mantle and ride states and a velocity-drive grab. A bot script climbs the S2 building while random blasts hit it, then grabs and throws debris at a wall. PASS: 10-minute randomised soak with zero stuck states (state watchdog), never inside a collider for more than 0.2 s, position always finite; a held 200 kg piece jitters < 2 cm; a thrown piece destroys a wall element through impact damage; the cat detaches or rides correctly in 100% of 'surface destroyed' events.

sources.name: Godot 4.7 documentation - retargeting and animation sharing
sources.covers: Godot specifics: BoneMap, SkeletonProfileHumanoid, shared AnimationLibrary, RetargetModifier3D
sources.license: Engine MIT; documentation CC BY 3.0
sources.automation: Agent-friendly: .import files and BoneMap .tres are plain text; reimport with godot --headless --import. Verify the exact .import key syntax on the first asset.
sources.formats: glTF/GLB preferred; FBX also imports
sources.best_items: Advanced Import Settings > select Skeleton3D > Retarget > bone_map = BoneMap with profile SkeletonProfileHumanoid (auto-maps common English bone names; magenta/red marks flag missing, duplicate or wrong-parent bones without blocking import). Remove Tracks: Except Bone Transform; Unimportant Positions (keeps only Root and Hips position); Unmapped Bones. Bone Renamer: Rename Bones; Unique Node (track paths independent of hierarchy). Rest Fixer: Apply Node Transform; Normalize Position Tracks (Hips height stored as motion_scale); Overwrite Axis (the key switch for sharing); Fix Silhouette with filter and base_height_adjustment. Reference pose: T-pose, facing +Z, +Y from parent to child joint. Import clip-only files as AnimationLibrary with the Remove Tracks options on; every retargeted character can then play the same libraries. Runtime alternative: RetargetModifier3D copies a parent skeleton's pose to child skeletons with different rests (profile, use_global_pose, position/rotation/scale flags).
sources.caveats: Overwrite Axis can give bad results when the original rests matter. Fix Silhouette cannot fix bone roll or large pose differences; feet may tilt on heeled models. Apply Node Transform can affect non-skeleton nodes. Tail and ear bones are outside the humanoid profile: shared clips never animate them (drive them procedurally) and 'Unmapped Bones' deletes their tracks from the cat's own clips. Keep root motion on the profile's Root bone; Mixamo has none.

sources.name: Godot 4.7 documentation - ragdolls, Jolt and skeleton modifiers
sources.covers: Godot specifics: PhysicalBoneSimulator3D ragdolls, Jolt joint limits, procedural modifiers
sources.license: Engine MIT; documentation CC BY 3.0
sources.automation: 'Create Physical Skeleton' is an editor button; a CLI-only agent should generate PhysicalBone3D nodes, shapes and joints from the humanoid bone names in a tool script and save one reusable template.
sources.best_items: PhysicalBoneSimulator3D under Skeleton3D with one PhysicalBone3D per simulated bone. Joints: Cone for shoulders, hips, neck (swing 20-90 deg, twist 20-45 deg); Hinge with angular limit for elbows and knees; default Pin crumples. Drop finger and helper bones. physical_bones_start_simulation(bone_names) for full or partial ragdoll, physical_bones_stop_simulation(), influence to blend with animation, physical_bones_add_collision_exception(). Because every retargeted NPC has identical bone names, one ragdoll template serves the whole crowd. Other modifiers listed in 4.7: SpringBoneSimulator3D (tail, ears), LookAtModifier3D, IKModifier3D with TwoBoneIK3D and ChainIK3D (feet, ledge hands), BoneConstraint3D, BoneTwistDisperser3D, LimitAngularVelocityModifier3D.
sources.caveats: Jolt is the default 3D physics for new projects; soft-limit joint properties (bias, softness, relaxation, damping, restitution, erp) are unsupported and only warn. Wrong bone names in the start list fail silently. Put ragdoll bodies and the CharacterBody3D capsule on separate layers. Each PhysicalBone3D costs performance: cap simultaneous ragdolls and freeze or pool them. Disable the AnimationTree while simulating. Jolt contact impulses are estimates. Modifiers run after the AnimationMixer.

assets_characters.recommendation: Honest baseline: no free cat is AAA. The best free meshes are indie/mobile grade (and I could not inspect them visually); AAA feel has to come from the animation system, fur/eye shading and game feel. Verdict: bipedal, humanoid-rigged, stylised cat. Why: Godot retargeting is built on SkeletonProfileHumanoid; every large free clip pool is humanoid (UAL1+2 free about 87 clips, Mesh2Motion 150+ CC0 GLBs, KayKit 161, Mixamo); grab, throw and wield need hands. A quadruped gets 12-21 clips, no carry/throw/weapon handling and nothing to retarget from. Route: (1) Little Cat mesh (one manual Sketchfab download). (2) BoneMap import; UAL1+2 for locomotion, jump, roll, slide, swim, melee, carry, overhand throw; Mesh2Motion for wall/ladder/pipe climb, ledge hang, wall run, three-point landing, freefall, ground pound, glide/fly, spells; Mixamo only for gaps (shimmy, vault, panic) or to auto-rig a fallback mesh. (3) Procedural layer: SpringBoneSimulator3D tail and ears, LookAtModifier3D, TwoBoneIK3D feet and ledge hands, lean, landing squash. (4) Hybrid only as a stretch goal on the same rig: all-fours sprint built from crawl clips plus IK; cut it if it looks wrong. Two meshes for two modes is not feasible without an artist. If a true four-legged cat is mandatory: Sphynx (CC BY), with powers via mouth, tail and telekinesis instead of held items. Install portable Blender for headless pose fixes, decimation and FBX-to-GLB. If budget ever appears: UAL1 Pro $9.99 + UAL2 Source $14.99 first, then a paid or commissioned cat.
license_traps: Sketchfab 'CC BY' on rips and fan art is worthless: the uploader cannot license IP they do not own. Seen in the cat results: 'An Animated Cat' by Evil_Katz (the cat from Murdered: Soul Suspect; description says it is not the uploader's), CatNap / Poppy Playtime, Meowscles (Fortnite), The Battle Cats, Yokai Watch, Pusheen, Hello Kitty, Talking Tom, Trevor Henderson's Cartoon Cat, Raid Shadow Legends 'Cat Ninja', Garry's Mod grabs. Only take models where the uploader states authorship and the design is original.

Third-party character designs: a modeller's CC BY does not clear someone else's concept. Examples: Knight Cat by muru (after a named ArtStation concept), Cat Witch and Persipia by AKM_Models (other artists' characters), House Cat (an illustrator's design), CuteLeaf scenes (credited original designs), Fab 'Cat Knight' (ArtStation concept), 'Kirana from Andalas' (unreleased studio game character).

NC / ND / SA licences: Cat Walk (CC BY-NC), Munchkin Cat (CC BY-NC-SA), WildPoly3D Squirrel (CC BY-NC; commercial only via Patreon), Animal Animator Pink Axolotl (CC BY-NC), Bandai Namco Research Motion Dataset (CC BY-NC 4.0), Ubisoft LAFAN1 (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0). ND also forbids re-rigging or retexturing. Filter Sketchfab API queries with license=by or license=cc0 and still read each page.

Mixamo: free and royalty-free inside games, but raw character/animation files may not be distributed (no public Git repo, no asset or template pack, no loose mod files) and may not be used to train ML models. Keep Mixamo-derived files in a private repo and ship them only inside the exported game.

CC BY obligations: ship a credits screen or file listing title, author, source URL, licence and a 'modified' note for every CC BY asset (the Sphynx Cat asks for 'Sphynx Cat by https://animalanimator.com'). Sketchfab Free Standard models may be used commercially but not redistributed as standalone assets, so keep their source files out of public repos.

Engine-locked content: Epic-published 'UE-Only' items on Fab (Epic sample projects, Paragon assets and similar) cannot be used in Godot even when free. Check the licence selector on every Fab listing; the free listings I opened showed a blank licence field in the fetched text.

Base-mesh generators: models built with DAZ3D/FaceGen (e.g. jungle_jim's 'Alina Ip') or Character Creator 4 (e.g. 'GameReadyCharacter_Day07_SpaceCat001') are uploaded as CC BY, but the underlying vendor base meshes generally may not be redistributed for free. Avoid.

AI-generated meshes (Sketchfab tags createdwithai, meshy, tripo3d; Fab 'Generated with AI: Yes', e.g. 'Free cat' by LapaModels): unclear copyright, generator free tiers impose their own licences, and Steam requires AI-content disclosure. Animal Animator's models may be AI-assisted (its site mentions 'sculpting + AI' for one model).
Meme cats (Maxwell / 'Dingus the cat', Pop Cat, OIIA cat, Boykisser, Bongo Cat): derived from real pets, photos or other artists' drawings; unsuitable as a commercial hero regardless of the CC label.

Extra author clauses: Cougar by SKYE bans NFT/crypto use; Kenney and KayKit ask that unmodified packs are not resold; Microsoft Rocketbox is MIT, so the copyright and licence notice must ship with the game; CMU mocap may be used in products but the data itself may not be resold.

Unstated or conflicting licences: Omabuarts 'Quirky Series - FREE Animals' shows no licence on its itch page (questions unanswered): free to download is not cleared for commercial use.
