UI art must be restyled (9-slice bases, input glyphs) to avoid the recognisable Kenney look. Particle and Smoke packs date from 2018 and 2014: fine for sparks, puffs and light cookies, not for hero explosions.

sources.name: OpenGameArt
sources.covers: Hobbyist SFX, music, 2D VFX sheets, textures, some 3D.
sources.license: Per asset: CC0, CC BY 3.0/4.0, CC BY-SA 3.0/4.0, OGA-BY 3.0/4.0, GPL 2/3, LGPL (from memory). Use CC0, CC BY and OGA-BY only.
sources.automation: No official API; files are normally direct links on each asset page (from memory). Every OpenGameArt URL returned HTTP 403 to the fetcher this session, so a script may be blocked by bot protection: plan for browser or human downloads.
sources.formats: WAV, OGG, MP3, FLAC, PNG, blend/OBJ/FBX.
sources.best_items: Not verifiable this session (from memory): '100 CC0 SFX' https://opengameart.org/content/100-cc0-sfx ; '100 CC0 metal and wood SFX' https://opengameart.org/content/100-cc0-metal-and-wood-sfx ; CC0 filter on https://opengameart.org/art-search-advanced for music loops and explosion sheets.
sources.caveats: VERDICT: USE WITH CARE, low priority. No page could be opened (403), so everything here is from memory. CC BY-SA and GPL items raise share-alike and anti-DRM questions for a closed Steam build. Quality is rarely AAA; Sonniss, itch CC0 packs and Unity flipbooks cover the same needs better.

sources.name: Pixabay (sound effects and music)
sources.covers: Large stock catalogue: gap-filling SFX (collapse, earthquake, crowd) and a very large trailer-style music catalogue (hybrid orchestral, epic, synthwave, dubstep).
sources.license: Pixabay Content License (Terms last updated 20 Oct 2026): irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, commercial and non-commercial use, modification allowed, attribution optional. Prohibited: selling or distributing content standalone (including via stock platforms), misleading or endorsement use, trademark use. Items published before 9 Jan 2019 are CC0.
sources.automation: None allowed: the Terms prohibit 'use of programs or robots for automatic data collection' and 'bulk, large-scale or systematic copying' without permission. Listing pages are readable, downloads are per-item buttons: human clicks only.
sources.formats: MP3 (from memory).
sources.style: Very mixed; many SFX are re-hosted Freesound material (account 'freesound_community').
sources.best_items: SFX search 'building collapse' (1,001 results) https://pixabay.com/sound-effects/search/building%20collapse/ - e.g. 'Exploding Building 1' and '2' (floraphonic), 'Earthquake Rumble & Cracking' (TheMediaGuy), 'Structure Crumbling - Traveling Echo in Deep Ruins' (Saturn-3-Music). Music search 'hybrid orchestral action' (22,414+ results) https://pixabay.com/music/search/hybrid%20orchestral%20action/ - e.g. 'Epic Hybrid (Main Title)' (Kulakovka), 'Powerful Orchestral Music Loop - Hybrid Action' (Sonican), 'Action (Synthwave)' (ARPMedia).
sources.caveats: VERDICT: USE WITH CARE (gap filler, not backbone). Licence is uploader-asserted: Pixabay gives no warranty and requires you to stop using content on a claim. AI-generated uploads exist and are supposed to be labelled. Keep a dated page snapshot per download. Whether audio downloads need an account was not confirmed.

sources.name: Mixkit
sources.covers: Small curated stock SFX sets (explosion, warfare, transport, animals, human, technology); stock music.
sources.license: Separate licences per item type: 'Mixkit Sound Effects Free License' and 'Mixkit Stock Music Free License'. Site text for SFX: royalty-free, 'can be used without attribution, plus no sign up is required', usable 'in both commercial and personal projects'.
sources.automation: No API; per-item 'Download Free SFX' buttons. Treat as browser clicks.
sources.formats: WAV for SFX and MP3 for music (from memory).

Categories listed: Transition, Nature, Technology, Animals, Transport, Human, Warfare, Game.
sources.caveats: VERDICT: SFX USE WITH CARE, MUSIC AVOID. Music FAQ (verified): 'You are not permitted to use Mixkit music in CDs, DVDs, Video Games or TV & Radio broadcasts.' The full SFX licence text could not be retrieved, so an explicit video-game clause for SFX is unverified. Low value next to Sonniss.

sources.name: CC BY 4.0 composer libraries: Incompetech and Scott Buckley (FreePD closed)
sources.covers: Finished music tracks: cinematic orchestral, hybrid, electronica, techno (Scott Buckley); very broad genre catalogue (Incompetech, https://incompetech.com/music/royalty-free/).
sources.license: CC BY 4.0 on both (verified). Incompetech credit: track title, 'Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com)', 'Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0' plus licence URL. Scott Buckley credit: '[Track Title] by Scott Buckley - released under CC-BY 4.0. www.scottbuckley.com.au'. Both sell no-attribution licences.
sources.automation: No API. Public per-track download pages; a script can fetch a hand-picked list of track URLs (exact file URL patterns not confirmed this session).

Scott Buckley: tracks must not be registered with Content ID, cannot be re-uploaded to streaming platforms, and his 'orchestral remixes' are excluded from CC ('at your own risk'). White Bat Audio (synthwave, https://whitebataudio.com/pages/license-agreement) is free with credit but asks to e-mail 'for sync licensing on major film and game projects' and bans AI training: get written permission before use.

sources.name: Free Music Archive (incl. artist HoliznaCC0)

Search rows do not show the licence: open each track page. The HoliznaCC0 page text says 'completely Public Domain' but the CC0 deed itself was not seen.

Tallbeard states NFT, AI training and resale of unmodified files are 'not endorsed'. Shapeforms forbids sharing the files in isolation. Most CC0 SFX packs on the listing are retro/8-bit and not useful here.

No confirmed motion-vector or normal maps: use frame blending and soft particles. Do not confuse with Unity Asset Store or VFX Graph sample content, which is not CC0.

sources.name: godotshaders.com
sources.covers: Community Godot shader snippets: glitch, matrix/code, smoke, fog, fire, explosion, distortion, dissolve.
sources.license: Per shader, chosen by the submitter: CC0, MIT or GNU GPL v3 (verified on https://godotshaders.com/license/). The licence covers code only; 'featured images, screenshots, videos and assets' are not covered.
sources.automation: Plain HTML pages with the code in a visible block; search via https://godotshaders.com/?s=<term>. No API; scraping individual pages works without login.

Licence not yet opened: '3D Glitch' https://godotshaders.com/shader/3d-glitch/ ; 'Distortion/Shockwave Shader' https://godotshaders.com/shader/distortion/ ; 'Alpha Erosion VisualShaderNode 4.4' https://godotshaders.com/shader/alpha-erosion-visualshadernode-4-4/
sources.caveats: VERDICT: USE WITH CARE. Check the line 'The shader code ... are under <licence>' on every page; the booleans assume CC0 picks (MIT needs its notice kept, GPL v3 must be skipped). Provenance is submitter-asserted: skip ports from Shadertoy or commercial games (a search hit was titled 'Balatro Original Fire Shader'). Many entries target Godot 3 or 4.0 and need porting.

sources.covers: Godot-native 3D VFX packs (explosions, hits, flames, electric, holograms, portals) with shaders, scenes and tool scripts; CC0 noise texture packs.

The stylised look must be re-tuned toward realism (noise scales, colour ramps, lighting). A Jan 2026 user report mentions shader errors in the Compatibility renderer.

sources.name: game-icons.net

NPS Yellowstone: 'recorded in the park and are in the public domain ... may be downloaded and used without limitation; however, please credit the National Park Service where appropriate'.

NASA: rockets, satellites, rovers for a landmark. NPS: wolves, elk, coyotes, ravens, bird and dawn choruses, thunder, fire, geysers and fumaroles (about 90 entries).

sources.style: Raw scans and scraped models; real-world map geometry.

sources.caveats: VERDICT: AVOID. OSM copyright page: 'If you alter or build upon our data, you may distribute the result only under the same licence', plus visible credit. A shipped city derived from OSM footprints can be argued to be a derivative database. A fictional, procedurally laid out medium map needs none of this; use real maps only as visual reference. Datasets carry NC or research-only terms or unvetted per-object licences, and scan meshes are poor inputs for fracture.

assets_misc.recommendation: AUDIO: backbone = Sonniss WAVs + CC0 fillers. Build each destruction event from layers picked by material x size: transient crack, body crumble, debris tail, sub/LFE (large only), dust/air; 5-8 variations per layer, AudioStreamRandomizer, +/-2 semitones, +/-3 dB; far variants = low-pass + distance delay. Cap voices per bus; replace swarms of small hits with one granular debris loop scaled by active fragments. Buses Music / Ambience / SFX (Destruction, Explosions, Foley, Cat) / UI into a limited Master; sidechain-duck Music and Ambience from Explosions; reverb and low-pass zones by depth; about -16 LUFS. Batch-prepare with ffmpeg + Python (trim, mono 48 kHz WAV one-shots, OGG loops, loudness per category). Rewind = pre-reversed copies; simulation edge = bit-crush bus + Glitch Noises. MUSIC: AudioStreamInteractive (beat/bar-synced transitions) driven by a chaos meter; fake stems by band-splitting when none exist; Sonniss braams as stingers. VFX: Forward+ renderer; each blast = light flash + HDR fireball flipbook + smoke column + dust ring + rigid chunks + GPU sparks + shockwave refraction + scorch/crack Decal + FogVolume haze + shake/hit-stop; pooled emitters. BOOKKEEPING: one manifest row per source file (path, pack, author, URL, licence + version, date, SHA-256, edits, credit string, saved licence page); originals in a private git-ignored tree; CI fails on unlisted assets or NC/ND/SA/GPL/engine-locked licences; generate the Credits screen and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES from it (CC BY: title, author, source, licence link, changes; OFL: licence text). AUTOMATION: no-login scripts = Sonniss, ambientCG, Poly Haven, Godot AssetLib API to GitHub zips (Kenney mirrors), GitHub repos (fonts, game-icons, KayKit, NASA, CC0 registry), Unity zips, Smithsonian/Met/Wikimedia APIs, godotshaders. Human click or login = itch.io, kenney.nl, Freesound, Pixabay, Mixkit, 99Sounds, FMA, Fab, Sketchfab, ZapSplat.
license_traps: Mixkit music: the site FAQ states 'You are not permitted to use Mixkit music in CDs, DVDs, Video Games or TV & Radio broadcasts' (verified). Only Mixkit SFX are candidates, and their explicit game clause is unverified.
BBC Sound Effects: RemArc licence covers personal, educational and research use only; commercial use needs a paid licence. Do not ship any of it.

Freesound: take CC0 only. CC BY-NC and legacy Sampling+ are unusable in a sold game; CC BY needs a per-sound credit. Record the licence shown on the download day and skip uploads that sound like film or game rips.

Sonniss, 99Sounds, Pixabay, Mixkit, Shapeforms and Fab all forbid redistributing the raw files. Consequences: private repo (or git-ignored sources), no loose audio folders in the build, no sound pack for modders, no source release that includes them. Sonniss additionally bans AI/ML training use and limits use to media production.

Sonniss licence changed to v2.0 on 27 Aug 2026 and the version published on the download day governs: licence text files inside older zips may be outdated, so archive the live licence page with the download date.

Pixabay: Terms (20 Oct 2026) ban robots and bulk copying, so no scripted harvesting; the licence is uploader-asserted with no warranty and you must stop using content if a claim arrives; AI-generated uploads exist. Keep a dated page snapshot per file and do not rely on Pixabay for anything central.

godotshaders.com: licence is per shader (CC0, MIT or GPL v3) and covers code only, not preview textures. Skip GPL v3 shaders, keep MIT notices, and skip ports from Shadertoy or commercial games (a search hit was titled 'Balatro Original Fire Shader') whatever licence the poster selected.

Engine-locked content: Unity-authored samples and some Asset Store content, and Epic 'UE-Only' content on Fab, cannot be used in Godot even when free. The 2016 Unity flipbook pack is the exception because it is explicitly CC0.
OpenGameArt: CC BY-SA and GPL items carry share-alike and anti-DRM questions for a closed Steam build; filter to CC0, CC BY and OGA-BY.
game-icons.net is CC BY 3.0 (only Viscious Speed and Zeromancer are CC0): every icon author used must be credited in the form 'Icons made by {author}. Available on https://game-icons.net'.

Google Fonts: OFL requires shipping the licence text and copyright notice with the game, forbids selling the font alone and forbids reusing a Reserved Font Name on modified files; the licence differs by folder (ofl/, apache/, ufl/).

CC BY music: Scott Buckley requires the exact credit form including 'released under CC-BY 4.0. www.scottbuckley.com.au', forbids Content ID registration and excludes his 'orchestral remixes' from the CC library. White Bat Audio's free licence asks to e-mail for major game projects and forbids AI training: get written permission or skip.
FreePD.com now shows 'permanently closed' (verified): do not pull its former catalogue from third-party mirrors whose licence cannot be proven.
Free Music Archive: licences are per track and include NC, ND, SA and the personal-only 'FMA-Limited'; search rows do not show the licence, so open every track page before use.

itch.io: the CC0 listing pages include paid packs and the site hosts many custom-licence packs; BinbunVFX Smoke/Impact/Fire packs and some Tiny Treats sets cost money. Check price, licence line and the generative-AI disclosure tag on each pack page.

OpenStreetMap: ODbL share-alike and attribution ('If you alter or build upon our data, you may distribute the result only under the same licence'). A city baked from OSM footprints can be argued to be a derivative database: build a fictional map instead.

Museum and government media: NASA insignia and logos are 'not in the public domain', no endorsement may be implied and astronaut likenesses need permission; Smithsonian is CC0 only where flagged; many other museums publish scans under non-commercial licences.

ambientCG has no crack or scorch decals (API queries returned 0 and 1 results): do not fill that gap with decals from textures.com-style sites or marketplace previews, whose free tiers forbid redistribution; generate them procedurally.
Polygonal Mind: the registry labels all collections CC0, but the 100Avatars GitHub README still restricts selling 'without any major modification'; store the CC0 proof next to the files.
Kenney mirrors in the Godot Asset Library are third-party repackages and can lag behind (Input Prompts mirror is v1.1, site is v1.5a): fine legally (CC0) but check versions.

'Royalty-free' is not a licence: YouTube Audio Library, Uppbeat or Bensound free tiers and similar are tied to videos, credits or subscriptions (from memory); do not use them in a game without reading the terms.

AI-generated audio (Pixabay items labelled AI-generated, AI music packs on itch.io) may trigger Steam and itch.io AI-content disclosure; prefer packs tagged 'No generative AI was used' (store policy details not checked).
